title: What we learned from a year of retrospectives

level1.from: Only then we read them out
options: Only then do we read them out
level1.note: 'Only then' at the start of a clause inverts the verb.

level2.from: Everyone agreed that communication could be better, nobody said what they actually ment by it, and we left with a list of action items that no one looked at again.
options: Everyone agreed that communication could be better, but nobody said what they actually meant by it, and we left with a list of action items that no one looked at again.
Everyone agreed that communication could be better. Nobody said what they meant by it, and the action items we left with were never looked at again.
level2.note: Three clauses in a row with no connective; the contrast between the first two is lost.

level2.from: Have to admit I was one of the talkers.
options: I have to admit I was one of the talkers.
I was one of the talkers, I admit.
level2.note: Missing subject — reads as a fragment.

level2.from: This sounds like a small thing but it changed who's voice got heard, because the quiet people had already committed there thoughts to paper before the loud ones could set the agenda.
options: This sounds like a small thing, but it changed whose voice got heard: the quiet people had already committed their thoughts to paper before the loud ones could set the agenda.
It sounds small, but it changed whose voice got heard. The quiet people had their thoughts on paper before the loud ones could set the agenda.
level2.note: The 'because' clause explains the whole sentence and wants a stronger break before it.

level2.from: It felt strange at first, we had so many ideas, but a single item that actually gets done is worth more then ten that get forgotten.
options: It felt strange at first, since we had so many ideas, but a single item that actually gets done is worth more than ten that get forgotten.
It felt strange at first — we had so many ideas — but one item that gets done is worth more than ten that get forgotten.
level2.note: Comma splice: 'we had so many ideas' is a full clause wedged between two others.

level2.from: The facilitator does not share their own points that session, they only make sure everyone else gets to.
options: The facilitator does not share their own points that session; they only make sure everyone else gets to.
The facilitator sits out that session and only makes sure everyone else gets to speak.

level2.from: This was less popular, some people really do not enjoy running meetings, but it broke the pattern of the same voices dominating and it gave everyone a feel for how hard it is to keep a discussion on track.
options: This was less popular, since some people really do not enjoy running meetings, but it broke the pattern of the same voices dominating and gave everyone a feel for how hard it is to keep a discussion on track.

This was less popular; some people really do not enjoy running meetings. But it broke the pattern of the same voices dominating, and everyone got a feel for how hard it is to keep a discussion on track.
level2.note: Comma splice, then two long clauses chained with 'and'.

level2.from: Not every retro is great, some are still flat, but the average has gone up alot and the action items now gets done more often then not.
options: Not every retro is great, and some are still flat, but the average has gone up a lot and the action items now get done more often than not.
Not every retro is great. Some are still flat, but the average has gone up a lot, and the action items now get done more often than not.
